positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Game Team: SoCal Slot Shop, San Diego, CA

When working with Bally Technology’s proprietary Alpha II SDK, C++ was the primary software language used. Much of the next generation Scientific Games SDK is centered around the Unity toolkit, with C# as its scripting language.

As a Game core library programmer, I primarily represented the interests of the remote San Diego studio. I fixed library bugs and implemented library enhancements as needed by the San Diego game teams. I also performed the same duties for other game teams who needed assistance. For example, I've added a WAV file parser to the Alpha II SDK that extracts cue markers so that bezel lighting animations can pulse to the beat of music. The Cher Live video slot machine demonstrates the capabilities I help add to the Alpha II C++ library.

As a lead programmer, my duties included working with the math department and game designers to agree upon the game mechanics and to work with the artists to develop a pipeline strategy. 

As a tools programmer, I have created scripts to streamline the workflow of the San Diego office, and I’ve created complex applications to improve the quality of games. For example, I’ve worked on stand alone C# apps that communicate with custom lighting hardware via Bally’s proprietary USB protocol. The apps are used by artists to design lighting animations and to export game ready data.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: I helped design and code the C++ user interface elements for two coin operated arcade games: H2Overdrive and Dirty Driving. I performed numerous miscellaneous tasks, such as the operator menus for H2Overdrive and its localization effort.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: As the Lead UI Programmer for the Redzone team, I helped design and implement a C++ UI front end for the PS2 game. The menu system was created with commercial SVG editors and trasnlated to game ready data. As a tools programmer for Redzone, I createdd a Win32 application to edit and export animation data. As a tools programmer for the NBA game, I designed and coded .NET TCP/IP tools to communicate between an in-house C# editor and the PS3 development computer. Also, I incorporated advanced features of the Matisse OO/DBMS system to develop a custom revision control system with bindings to a .NET application. I helped the UI team with their Anark export effort, which often included localization. As the NBA tools programmer, I maintained the LAN C++ build system. The system included MIcrosoft JScript and ActiveX components that compiled the game, ran unit test programs, and appended the results to an LAN web server.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Developed an animation compression system for Gravity Games, Bike Vert., which included a Maya exporter/compressor and decompression logic. Developed a compiler that converts an animation blend script (at game load time) into the required binary representation. Developed a nightly build systems for Weasel. Worked with artists and animators to bugs and augment various in house tools, which included Maya plugins, MEL scripts, Win32 GUI programming. Developed a low level network (TCP/IP) communications prototype for the PS2. Provided real-time in-game feedback concerning objects racing around tracks.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer / Analyst
positions.description:
Summary
Technical lead for single teams and coordinator of multiple teams developing military critical awareness software. Designed and coded TC/IP and CORBA client-server apps in C++ and Java, RDBMS schema and SQL queries. Designed and coded Win32 and Java Swing front-end interfaces.

Detailed Descriptions
VANANERA/BrowseCutter. Responsible for all C++ components in the Audio-Video media ingestion products, which include the Video Archive News Agent (VANA), Video Exploitation Remote Access (VERA), and BroWseCutterTM products. Created software that manipulates MPEG, JPEG, HTML, and RDBMS data. The AV media required a strong background in C++, Java, multi-threaded algorithms, ODBC, MPEG, JPEG, and HTML. Additional tasks included an ODBC interfaces, various MFC GUI windows, and socket communication. 

DARPA’s Next Generation Infomation Infrastructure (NGII).  System Integration Team Lead. Managed the team that created the Install Shield application for the NGII software suite. 

Object Model Foundation Group (OMFG). System Integration Lead /Team Software Lead.  Responsible for the software design and integration of the Schema Server component with CORBA applets, RMI servers, CORBA servers, and Rational Rose OLE components.

Map Based Planning (MBP) Integration Coordinator/ Programmer. Led and coordinated the joint-company task of moving the MBP system integration from the JDEF to NRaD.

Integration Coordinator/ Support.  AdditionalMap Based Planning (MBP) Duties. I Represented SAIC, San Diego at the JDEF.  Integrated and adapted a JRAMS version specifically for MBP.

Joint Readiness Automated Management System (JRAMS). Sponsored by The Atlantic Command (ACOM). Responsible for designing and programming a Joint Staff force readiness assessment tool called JRAMS. JRAMS uses the Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA) technology to merge data from various military databases and present the force readiness results in a non­technical GUI application.
